raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Addresses #58726.

On integrated GPUs (DGX Spark / GB10), the shared weight loaders copy each checkpoint tensor to the GPU with `param.copy_(loaded_weight)` straight from the safetensors mmap view. For a contiguous, same-dtype source, PyTorch passes that pageable pointer directly to the driver copy, so the page faults happen inside the copy. On GB10 that is several times slower than faulting the same pages on the CPU first: 1.7–3.0 ms vs 0.08–0.64 ms per 800 KiB tensor in #58726. `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` has at least 140k such tensors, and its main weight load takes 452 s from NFS and 475 s from local NVMe.

This adds `copy_weight_(dst, src)` to `vllm/model_executor/utils.py`. On an integrated GPU it touches one byte per page of `src`, then runs `dst.copy_(src)`. It is used at the 26 copy sites of the shared loaders: `linear.py` (8), `parameter.py` (6), `routed_experts.py` (8), `vocab_parallel_embedding.py` (2) and `default_weight_loader` (2).

- **Gate:** `current_platform.is_integrated_gpu()` for a CUDA destination, cached per device. On a discrete Ada Lovelace GPU the same micro-benchmark shows the plain copy is fastest in every cache state, and the touch adds 0.022–0.028 ms per tensor, so it stays off there. When off, the extra checks cost ~0.46 µs per call (0.91 vs 0.45 µs for a 16-byte CPU copy), about 0.14 s per 300k tensors.
- **Only contiguous, same-dtype CPU sources are touched.** Non-contiguous or dtype-converting copies already go through a CPU temporary in PyTorch (`copy_requires_temporaries` in `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Copy.cu`), which faults the pages on the CPU.
- **Why at the copy site rather than in `safetensors_weights_iterator`** (discussed with @gitbisector in #58726):
  - Under TP each rank touches only the slice it copies. A prefault in the iterator read whole tensors: ~287 GiB per rank on DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4, and a slower load at the default `read_ahead_kb=128`.
  - The touch runs right before the copy, so a consumer that buffers the weight stream can't have the pages evicted in between.
  - Tensors a model serves from the mapping (#58439) are never copied, so they are never touched, and no size cap is needed.
- **Not covered:** model-specific loaders that call `.copy_()` or `.to(device)` themselves keep today's behaviour until they call the helper. Its docstring says to. @stecasta routed one such out-of-tree expert loader through it: ~55 GiB of copies moved onto the touch path, and its weight loading took about 70% less time.
- **Measured only on GB10** (TP=1 below, TP=4 by @gitbisector). Other integrated devices, such as Jetson Orin / Thor, will take the touch path but are untested. I haven't checked what GH200 reports as `is_integrated`; if it reports 0, nothing changes there.

## Test Plan

- New tests in `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`:
  - `test_copy_weight_prefault_copies_exact_bytes`: with the gate forced on, the helper accepts 0-d, empty, bf16, fp8 and dim-1-narrowed sources and copies them byte for byte. CI has no integrated GPU, so this is the only coverage of that path.
  - `test_copy_weight_prefault_maps_the_mmap_view`: after the call, every page of a safetensors view is mapped (`/proc/self/smaps` Rss of the file mapping). With the touch disabled it fails: 64 KiB mapped vs 4 MiB.
- Existing CPU-runnable loader tests, before and after the change.
- `pre-commit` on the changed files, including `mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual`.
- Boot A/B on a DGX Spark.

```bash
# CPU only, repo on PYTHONPATH inside vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 (torch 2.13.0+cu130), no GPU
docker run --rm -v $PWD:/w:ro -e PYTHONPATH=/w -w /w --entrypoint bash vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 -c \
  "uv pip install --system -q tblib pytest && python3 -m pytest -q \
   tests/model_executor/test_utils.py \
   tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py tests/kernels/moe/test_fp8_tp_loading.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_tying.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py"

pre-commit run --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed files>
```

## Test Result

- `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`: 18 passed (12 existing, 6 new).
- Loader tests: 216 passed, 5 skipped. 38 tests fail with and without the change, the same set on both, all because the container has no GPU:
  - 18 error at setup with `Failed to infer device type`.
  - 18 `test_reload` cases fail because `current_platform.device_count` is `None`.
  - 2 `test_fp8_tp_default_keeps_refined_layout[*-triton]` cases can't confirm the Triton kernel, so the layer pads its TP shard instead of refining the block shape.
- `pre-commit` and `mypy-3.12` passed.

### Boot A/B, DGX Spark (GB10), TP=1

Nine full server boots of `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, interleaved, with the client page cache for the checkpoint dropped before each one.

- **Build:** the image is vLLM v0.30.0 plus out-of-tree patches, not `main`. The helper is copied from this branch and applied to v0.30.0's copies of the same files (25 sites; v0.30.0's `_load_w2` has no chunk loop). It predates a cleanup that renamed the gate function and dropped a redundant `numel() > 0` check, which doesn't change behaviour here. A counting wrapper, not part of this PR, logged the gate and how many copies were touched.
- **Out-of-tree patches on in every arm:** the expert-name index (= #58720, merged), an MTP name prefilter, and the PLE table served from the mapping (never copied).
- **Storage:** NFS with the client's `read_ahead_kb` at 16384, or local NVMe at the default 128.

| loader | storage | main load (s) | MTP load (s) | start → `/health` (s) | swapped out, start → KV profile (GiB) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| stock | NFS | 451.8 | 36.1 | 584 | 4.4 |
| this PR (3 boots) | NFS | 25.9 / 27.0 / 28.0 | 0.8 | 124–129 | 3.6–4.3 |
| stock | NVMe | 475.2 | 31.7 | 609 | 4.2 |
| this PR (2 boots) | NVMe | 46.4 / 54.5 | 2.6–2.9 | 149–153 | 3.2–4.0 |
| *out-of-tree, for reference: `pread` tensors ≤ 64 MiB in the iterator, clone / chunked copy above that* | NFS / NVMe | 21.0 / 88.5 | 1.2 / 1.3 | 113 / 179 | 0 / 0 |

- The gate logged `cuda:0 = True` in every boot with this PR. By the counter's last line (140,000 calls), 139,965 copies (63.4 GiB) had been touched. The other 35 were copies PyTorch stages through a CPU temporary anyway.
- Greedy outputs (5 prompts × 400 tokens, temperature 0) and first-token logprobs are identical in all nine boots, and decode speed is unchanged. No accuracy eval was run here: the touch only reads the source, so the loaded weights are byte-identical (unit test above). @stecasta's GSM8K run is below.
- Swap: loading from mmap views pushes 3.2–4.4 GiB of other memory to swap on this 128 GB machine, and stock loading does it as much as this PR. The pread variant doesn't map the files and doesn't swap. vLLM counts the swapped-out memory as free when it sizes the KV cache. I haven't looked into why the kernel swaps here.

### TP=1, warm cache (from @hclsys, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-5919067348))

`Qwen3-1.7B` on one GB10, `load_format=safetensors`, `enforce_eager`, page cache warm, fresh process per run, this branch vs its merge-base `77871126f9`.

| | `Loading weights took` | `LLM()` init |
|---|---:|---:|
| merge-base (3 runs) | 20.2–23.7 s | 44.4–54.8 s |
| this PR (2 runs) | 0.50 / 0.69 s | 26.3 / 29.4 s |

The third base run came after the PR runs, so the difference isn't cache order. With the cache warm the time isn't disk reads but the faults taken through a fresh mapping during the copy. On a discrete RTX PRO 6000 the touch makes no difference, ~0.1 ms per tensor either way (@gitbisector, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58726#issuecomment-5918595410)).

### TP=1, cold cache (from @stecasta, [review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#pullrequestreview-5496877797))

`nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` with a DFlash2 drafter on one GB10, v0.31.0 plus internal patches with this PR applied as a Python overlay. Checkpoint on local disk (`read_ahead_kb=128`), page cache dropped before every boot, two boots per arm.

| | `Loading weights took`, main model | `Model loading took` | start → `/health` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| stock | 96.5 / 96.7 s | 122 / 122 s | 595 / 591 s |
| this PR | 9.5 / 9.8 s | 16 / 16 s | 486 / 486 s |

GSM8K-256 with this PR: 244/256, in line with stock. Minimum `MemAvailable` (~38.5 GiB) and peak swap (0.5 GiB) during load were the same in both arms.

### TP=4 (from @gitbisector, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-5852543296))

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on four GB10s, this PR ported to a v0.28.1-based build (25 of the 26 sites), load-only boots, page cache dropped before each, arms interleaved. Times are `Model loading took` on the slowest rank.

| `read_ahead_kb` | boots | stock | this PR | read per rank vs stock |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 3 + 3 | 192–195 s | 156–161 s (−18%) | +0–8 GiB |
| 128 | 3 + 3 | 205–207 s | 149–151 s (−27%) | +0–8 GiB |
| 1024, consumer that sorts the stream | 1 + 1 | 248 s | 225 s | +2–10 GiB |

At 128 the iterator-level prefault made this load slower (202 → 241 s) because every rank read whole tensors (~287 GiB); at the copy site each rank reads about what stock reads. Most of the gain is the slowest rank catching up: in stock, the ranks holding slices 0 and 2 lag by 25–60 s on small same-dtype slices (expert scales, FP8 attention rows). The routed experts there are `I8` loaded into `uint8` params, a converting copy that PyTorch already stages on the CPU, so the helper touches 5.6 of 72.3 GiB per rank.

## Duplicate-work check

- No open PR references #58726; searches for "prefault", "integrated gpu weight loading" and "mmap page fault copy" found none that change these copy sites.
- #49991 (ROCm, clones in the iterator behind an env flag, for a KFD copy-on-write issue) and #50794 (Ascend, clones before the H2D copy to avoid a DMA hang) handle the same copies on other platforms, for different causes.
- #57973 (safetensors prefetch loader) and #55985 (fastsafetensors fit planner) are alternative load paths.
- #58857 / #58782 remove the `sorted()` buffering in the DeepSeek-V4 VL wrappers; complementary to this.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5.5): implementation, tests, the boot A/B scripts, and a draft of this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and boots above on my own machines.

The slice-position finding also explains why the direct saving is small on your ranks 1 and 3: most of your bytes are the `I8` → `uint8` experts, which take PyTorch's converting path and already fault on the CPU. On Qwen3.8 the experts are same-dtype, so nearly everything goes through the touch.

|---|---|---|---|
| stock | 504.9 / 534.0 s | 62.6 / 54.4 s | 575 / 599 s |
| #58868 | **65.9 / 64.9 s** | 41.4 / 32.5 s | **121 / 111 s** |

- **Metric:** vLLM's own "Loading weights took" lines.
- **Output:** the greedy output hash is identical across all four starts.
- **Not measured:** discrete GPUs, TP>1, NFS.

Data: [ld58868.txt](https://github.com/jschmied/qwen38-flash-next-gb10/blob/10d2b9df7c2bb2178039393abe5e4211a8cc4f27/notes/data/ld58868/ld58868.txt), write-up [§5w](https://github.com/jschmied/qwen38-flash-next-gb10/blob/10d2b9df7c2bb2178039393abe5e4211a8cc4f27/notes/speed-of-light.md#5w-weight-loading-vllm58868-cuts-the-main-load-87--505534-s--6566-s-model-loading-575599-s--111121-s).

Written with AI assistance (Claude Code).

Ran this end-to-end on a GB10 (DGX Spark, sm_121, CUDA 13). Qwen3-1.7B, `load_format=safetensors`, TP1, `enforce_eager`, page cache warm, fresh process per run, your branch vs its own merge-base so the patch is the only difference:

```
                           Loading weights took     LLM() init
base 77871126f9            23.48 / 20.18 / 23.66 s  54.8 / 44.4 / 46.7 s
+ this PR 857f70df4b        0.50 / 0.69 s            26.3 / 29.4 s
```

~30x on the load itself, ~1.6x on total engine init for a 3.4 GB model.

I ran base twice, then the PR, then base a third time — that last one is still 23.66 s, so it isn't cache ordering.

Separately, @gitbisector ran the standalone `mmap -> copy_` A/B on a discrete sm_120 and the touch makes no difference there (~0.1 ms/tensor either way), while on this card it's 4.9 ms vs 0.12. I'd taken the other side of that on #58726 and was wrong — the `is_integrated_gpu()` gate is doing real work, not narrowing a general win.

Verified `copy_weight_ present = True/False` per run before trusting either leg.

@Willian-Zhang here are the TP4 numbers I promised on #58726. Setup: `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, TP4 + DCP2 across four GB10s, weights on local NVMe ext4, page cache dropped on every node before every boot. One boot per cell.

The image is a vLLM fork at `8a728663c`, so I ported #58868 by hand. Two hunks didn't apply: the `_load_w2` tail copy (the pre-chunking version) and the `utils.py` imports. In this model, all weight copies go through `copy_weight_` except the `attn_sink` scalars.

Target weights pass, "Loading weights took", per rank:

| `--load-format auto` | `read_ahead_kb=1024` | `read_ahead_kb=128` |
|---|---|---|
| stock | 130–160 s (mean 146) | 114–168 s (mean 140) |
| + #58868 | 106–132 s (mean 122) | 104–119 s (mean 112) |

So #58868 is about 20% faster here, against the ~30× hclsys measured on Qwen3-1.7B. Readahead makes little difference either way at TP4. I haven't looked into where the rest of the `auto` time goes. Ranks within a cell spread by up to ±25 s, so read 20% as approximate.

For comparison, `--load-format fastsafetensors` took 52–58 s on the same model and nodes when I measured it earlier (read with O_DIRECT, so readahead doesn't apply). Our production config adds per-rank slice reads and comes in at 43–45 s, but that's an out-of-tree change, not something you'd get from upstream.

None of this argues against the PR. It fixes the GB10 fault cost and is clearly a win. It just doesn't close most of the gap for large TP-sharded MoE checkpoints.

Thanks @gitbisector. These don't line up with your [09-27 numbers](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-5852543296), which are the ones the description cites now:

| | 09-27 | today |
|---|---|---|
| build | 0.28.1-based, 25 of 26 sites | fork at `8a728663c`, 2 hunks not applied |
| metric | `Model loading took`, slowest rank | `Loading weights took`, per rank |
| boots | 3 + 3, interleaved | 1 per cell |
| stock → this PR, `read_ahead_kb=1024` | 192–195 → 156–161 s (−18%) | 130–160 → 106–132 s |
| stock → this PR, `read_ahead_kb=128` | 205–207 → 149–151 s (−27%) | 114–168 → 104–119 s |
| `fastsafetensors` | ~88 s | 52–58 s |

On 09-27, 128 was slower than 1024 in stock and gained more from the touch, while today readahead makes little difference. And `fastsafetensors` went from ~88 s to 52–58 s. Did something else change between the two runs, like the nodes, kernel, readahead on all four nodes, or the image? Which set should the description use? I'll update it once I know.

On the size of the gain, I think the gap to hclsys's ~30× comes from coverage. In your 09-27 run the helper touched 5.6 of 72.3 GiB per rank. The `I8` routed experts do go through `copy_weight_`, but the same-dtype check skips the touch for them, since the converting copy already reads the source on the CPU. hclsys's Qwen3-1.7B run is TP1, all bf16 and warm, so every byte takes the touch. So I agree with your conclusion: this fixes the GB10 fault cost and isn't aimed at the rest of a cold TP-sharded MoE load.

@hclsys thanks for the TP1 run, I've added it to the description.

@Willian-Zhang you're right, and nothing changed between the runs. I changed the metric and then compared across it, which is my mistake. Use the 09-27 set: 3+3 interleaved boots, slowest rank, `Model loading took`.

Both runs used the same build and nodes. "0.28.1-based" in the 09-27 comment and "fork at `8a728663c`" are the same image (`0.28.1rc1.dev388+g8a728663c`). The two hunks that didn't apply this time I ported by hand, so coverage matches 09-27's 25 of 26 sites. The chunked `_load_w2` branch doesn't exist in that version. Readahead was set explicitly on all four nodes for every boot.

Here are last night's single boots on the 09-27 metric:

| `Model loading took`, slowest rank | 09-27 (3+3 boots) | 09-30 (1 boot) |
|---|---|---|
| stock, `read_ahead_kb=1024` | 192–195 s | 197 s |
| #58868, `read_ahead_kb=1024` | 156–161 s | 166 s (−16%) |
| stock, `read_ahead_kb=128` | 205–207 s | 206 s |
| #58868, `read_ahead_kb=128` | 149–151 s | 155 s (−25%) |

They agree. So does the readahead effect: at 128, stock is slower and #58868 gains more. My "readahead makes little difference" came from averaging per-rank times, which hides the slow ranks (slices 0 and 2) that 09-27 explained. Please disregard that sentence.

`fastsafetensors` is also one measurement under two metrics. ~88 s is `Model loading took`, and 52–58 s is the target `Loading weights took` from the same runs. I should have labelled which one I quoted.

Agreed on coverage. That matches the 5.6 of 72.3 GiB in the 09-27 comment.
Thanks for going back and re-running these on the same metric, that clears it up. The description already uses the 09-27 numbers, so I'll leave it as is.

Thanks @stecasta for the cold-cache run and the GSM8K check. I've added both to the description.

Agreed on the docstring. 66d42b06d adds a line saying model-specific loaders should call `copy_weight_` instead of `.copy_()` when they copy a checkpoint tensor to the device, and that off integrated GPUs it's a plain `copy_`, so it's safe to call everywhere. I've also put your out-of-tree loader result under "Not covered" as an example.

- **Measured only on GB10** (TP=1 below, TP=4 by @gitbisector). Other integrated devices, such as Jetson Orin / Thor, will take the touch path but are untested. I haven't checked what GH200 reports as `is_integrated`; if it reports 0, nothing changes there.

## Test Plan

- New tests in `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`:
  - `test_copy_weight_prefault_copies_exact_bytes`: with the gate forced on, the helper accepts 0-d, empty, bf16, fp8 and dim-1-narrowed sources and copies them byte for byte. CI has no integrated GPU, so this is the only coverage of that path.
  - `test_copy_weight_prefault_maps_the_mmap_view`: after the call, every page of a safetensors view is mapped (`/proc/self/smaps` Rss of the file mapping). With the touch disabled it fails: 64 KiB mapped vs 4 MiB.
- Existing CPU-runnable loader tests, before and after the change.
- `pre-commit` on the changed files, including `mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual`.
- Boot A/B on a DGX Spark.

```bash
# CPU only, repo on PYTHONPATH inside vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 (torch 2.13.0+cu130), no GPU
docker run --rm -v $PWD:/w:ro -e PYTHONPATH=/w -w /w --entrypoint bash vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 -c \
  "uv pip install --system -q tblib pytest && python3 -m pytest -q \
   tests/model_executor/test_utils.py \
   tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py tests/kernels/moe/test_fp8_tp_loading.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_tying.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py"

pre-commit run --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed files>
```

## Test Result

- `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`: 18 passed (12 existing, 6 new).
- Loader tests: 216 passed, 5 skipped. 38 tests fail with and without the change, the same set on both, all because the container has no GPU:
  - 18 error at setup with `Failed to infer device type`.
  - 18 `test_reload` cases fail because `current_platform.device_count` is `None`.
  - 2 `test_fp8_tp_default_keeps_refined_layout[*-triton]` cases can't confirm the Triton kernel, so the layer pads its TP shard instead of refining the block shape.
- `pre-commit` and `mypy-3.12` passed.

### Boot A/B, DGX Spark (GB10), TP=1

Nine full server boots of `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, interleaved, with the client page cache for the checkpoint dropped before each one.

- **Build:** the image is vLLM v0.30.0 plus out-of-tree patches, not `main`. The helper is copied from this branch and applied to v0.30.0's copies of the same files (25 sites; v0.30.0's `_load_w2` has no chunk loop). It predates a cleanup that renamed the gate function and dropped a redundant `numel() > 0` check, which doesn't change behaviour here. A counting wrapper, not part of this PR, logged the gate and how many copies were touched.
- **Out-of-tree patches on in every arm:** the expert-name index (= #58720, merged), an MTP name prefilter, and the PLE table served from the mapping (never copied).
- **Storage:** NFS with the client's `read_ahead_kb` at 16384, or local NVMe at the default 128.

| loader | storage | main load (s) | MTP load (s) | start → `/health` (s) | swapped out, start → KV profile (GiB) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| stock | NFS | 451.8 | 36.1 | 584 | 4.4 |
| this PR (3 boots) | NFS | 25.9 / 27.0 / 28.0 | 0.8 | 124–129 | 3.6–4.3 |
| stock | NVMe | 475.2 | 31.7 | 609 | 4.2 |
| this PR (2 boots) | NVMe | 46.4 / 54.5 | 2.6–2.9 | 149–153 | 3.2–4.0 |
| *out-of-tree, for reference: `pread` tensors ≤ 64 MiB in the iterator, clone / chunked copy above that* | NFS / NVMe | 21.0 / 88.5 | 1.2 / 1.3 | 113 / 179 | 0 / 0 |

- The gate logged `cuda:0 = True` in every boot with this PR. By the counter's last line (140,000 calls), 139,965 copies (63.4 GiB) had been touched. The other 35 were copies PyTorch stages through a CPU temporary anyway.
- Greedy outputs (5 prompts × 400 tokens, temperature 0) and first-token logprobs are identical in all nine boots, and decode speed is unchanged. No accuracy eval was run here: the touch only reads the source, so the loaded weights are byte-identical (unit test above). @stecasta's GSM8K run is below.
- Swap: loading from mmap views pushes 3.2–4.4 GiB of other memory to swap on this 128 GB machine, and stock loading does it as much as this PR. The pread variant doesn't map the files and doesn't swap. vLLM counts the swapped-out memory as free when it sizes the KV cache. I haven't looked into why the kernel swaps here.

### TP=1, warm cache (from @hclsys, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-5919067348))

`Qwen3-1.7B` on one GB10, `load_format=safetensors`, `enforce_eager`, page cache warm, fresh process per run, this branch vs its merge-base `77871126f9`.

| | `Loading weights took` | `LLM()` init |
|---|---:|---:|
| merge-base (3 runs) | 20.2–23.7 s | 44.4–54.8 s |
| this PR (2 runs) | 0.50 / 0.69 s | 26.3 / 29.4 s |

The third base run came after the PR runs, so the difference isn't cache order. With the cache warm the time isn't disk reads but the faults taken through a fresh mapping during the copy. On a discrete RTX PRO 6000 the touch makes no difference, ~0.1 ms per tensor either way (@gitbisector, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58726#issuecomment-5918595410)).

### TP=1, cold cache (from @stecasta, [review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#pullrequestreview-5496877797))

`nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` with a DFlash2 drafter on one GB10, v0.31.0 plus internal patches with this PR applied as a Python overlay. Checkpoint on local disk (`read_ahead_kb=128`), page cache dropped before every boot, two boots per arm.

| | `Loading weights took`, main model | `Model loading took` | start → `/health` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| stock | 96.5 / 96.7 s | 122 / 122 s | 595 / 591 s |
| this PR | 9.5 / 9.8 s | 16 / 16 s | 486 / 486 s |

GSM8K-256 with this PR: 244/256, in line with stock. Minimum `MemAvailable` (~38.5 GiB) and peak swap (0.5 GiB) during load were the same in both arms.

### TP=4 (from @gitbisector, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-5852543296))

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on four GB10s, this PR ported to a v0.28.1-based build (25 of the 26 sites), load-only boots, page cache dropped before each, arms interleaved. Times are `Model loading took` on the slowest rank.

| `read_ahead_kb` | boots | stock | this PR | read per rank vs stock |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 3 + 3 | 192–195 s | 156–161 s (−18%) | +0–8 GiB |
| 128 | 3 + 3 | 205–207 s | 149–151 s (−27%) | +0–8 GiB |
| 1024, consumer that sorts the stream | 1 + 1 | 248 s | 225 s | +2–10 GiB |

At 128 the iterator-level prefault made this load slower (202 → 241 s) because every rank read whole tensors (~287 GiB); at the copy site each rank reads about what stock reads. Most of the gain is the slowest rank catching up: in stock, the ranks holding slices 0 and 2 lag by 25–60 s on small same-dtype slices (expert scales, FP8 attention rows). The routed experts there are `I8` loaded into `uint8` params, a converting copy that PyTorch already stages on the CPU, so the helper touches 5.6 of 72.3 GiB per rank.

## Duplicate-work check

- No open PR references #58726; searches for "prefault", "integrated gpu weight loading" and "mmap page fault copy" found none that change these copy sites.
- #49991 (ROCm, clones in the iterator behind an env flag, for a KFD copy-on-write issue) and #50794 (Ascend, clones before the H2D copy to avoid a DMA hang) handle the same copies on other platforms, for different causes.
- #57973 (safetensors prefetch loader) and #55985 (fastsafetensors fit planner) are alternative load paths.
- #58857 / #58782 remove the `sorted()` buffering in the DeepSeek-V4 VL wrappers; complementary to this.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5.5): implementation, tests, the boot A/B scripts, and a draft of this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and boots above on my own machines.

Times are `Model loading took` on the slowest rank. The copy site keeps the gain without the iterator version's TP over-read (~287 GiB per rank here), and it holds up under a consumer that buffers the stream.

Most of that gain comes from TP slice position, which fits the PR. In stock, ranks 0 and 2 finish 25–60 s after ranks 1 and 3. A per-slice benchmark on all four nodes shows the lag follows the slice, not the node: slices 0 and 2 load 1.3–2.2 s slower per two shards on every node. The slow part is the small same-dtype slices (the expert scales and FP8 attention rows) that the driver faults in from a cold cache. With the touch, all four slices take the same time, so the slowest rank catches up. The direct saving on ranks 1 and 3 is about 10 s.

Coverage: on this checkpoint the helper touches 5.6 of 72.3 GiB per rank. The 64.7 GiB of routed experts are stored as `I8` and loaded into `uint8` params, so the dtype gate skips them. That's correct: the converting copy already faults on the CPU, and at 128 it was faster in a micro-benchmark than touch-then-copy.

For comparison, `--load-format fastsafetensors` reads with O_DIRECT, so neither readahead nor these page faults apply to it. On the same model and nodes it loads in ~88 s against 156–161 s here. On unified memory it needs #55985 (ours) plus some fastsafetensors fixes that aren't upstream yet.

Hi @Willian-Zhang, thanks for the contribution.

LGTM. We reproduced it on a DGX Spark (GB10, TP1). The build is v0.31.0 plus internal patches; the PR applied cleanly as a Python overlay. Same node, page cache dropped before every boot, checkpoint already on local disk (`read_ahead_kb` 128), two boots per arm:

| Model | `Loading weights took`, main model | `Model loading took` | start to `/health` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` + DFlash2 drafter, stock | 96.5 / 96.7 s | 122 / 122 s | 595 / 591 s |

GSM8K-256 on the PR arm is 244/256, in line with stock. Minimum `MemAvailable` (~38.5 GiB) and peak swap (0.5 GiB) during load were the same with and without the PR.

We also tried a model whose routed experts are loaded by an out-of-tree loader that calls `.copy_()` itself, the "not covered" case in your description. Routing that one call through `copy_weight_` moved ~55 GiB of copies onto the touch path and cut its weight loading by about 70%, so the helper carries over to other loaders as soon as they call it.

Minor: since `copy_weight_` is the entry point for this, a line in its docstring saying that model-specific loaders should use it instead of `.copy_()` for host-to-device weight copies would help the next loader author find it.
